entries.title: NSA/CISA/FBI/EPA/DOE Joint Advisory: AI Is Lowering the Bar for ICS Attacks on US Critical Infrastructure
entries.summary: A five-agency US advisory warns that unidentified threat actors are using AI to generate exploitation scripts targeting Siemens PLCs across energy, water, food, and manufacturing sectors — the first multi-agency statement directly linking AI tooling to active industrial control system attacks.

entries.title: Kriminal: Commodity Criminal AI Service Sells Guardrail Bypass for $12.99/Month, Wrapping Grok, Claude, Mistral, and Llama 3.3
entries.summary: ThreatDown researchers identified a clearnet criminal AI service offering uncensored exploit development, OSINT, and social engineering through named agent personas starting at $12.99/month, demonstrating that provider-level safety controls can be systematically circumvented at commodity cost.

entries.title: Darktrace Report: Frontier AI Agents Can Now Autonomously Build and Execute Multi-Stage Attack Chains
entries.summary: Darktrace's State of AI Cybersecurity 2026 report, drawing on original threat data, documents that frontier AI agents with sufficient autonomy can independently develop and execute multi-stage attack chains — including social engineering, supply-chain compromise, and deception — against real targets, marking this as an active rather than theoretical risk.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.19857: LLMs Inadvertently Leak In-Context Secrets via Ordinary Outputs — More Capable Models Leak More
entries.summary: Across eight proprietary models, 2-digit in-context secrets are reconstructed with near-perfect accuracy and 4-digit secrets at 82% exact match from outputs produced in response to ordinary, non-adversarial requests; stronger instruction-following amplifies leakage, an RL-trained adversary extracts full Social Security Numbers from a production-style agent, and a classifier infers health/financial predicates from routine text — suggesting context leakage is a byproduct of capability, not a patchable bug.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.20055 (EchoCoT): Hidden Chain-of-Thought Extracted from Black-Box Frontier LRMs at Up to 66.4% Near-Verbatim Success via API
entries.summary: EchoCoT exploits a previously overlooked reasoning-replay surface between tool calls to iteratively extract hidden chain-of-thought traces from frontier proprietary large reasoning models — achieving up to 66.4% near-verbatim extraction on open-source models and extracting 33,463 tokens from a 32,948-token target on Gemini-2.5 — establishing hidden-CoT theft as a practical IP and security risk.

entries.title: Critical Sandbox Escape in isolated-vm Exposes AI Agent Platforms Including n8n, Sim.ai, Mastra, and Activepieces
entries.summary: A type confusion vulnerability in isolated-vm — a JavaScript sandboxing library downloaded more than 1 million times weekly and embedded in popular AI agent and automation platforms — enables sandbox escape and potential remote code execution; patched versions 7.0.1 and 6.2.0 are available.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.16895: Frontier AI Companies' Self-Selected Risk Frameworks Leave 'Orphan Risks' — Including Harmful Manipulation — Unaddressed
entries.summary: Comparing Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and Meta safety and compliance documents from 2023–2026, the paper identifies four filters (measurability, severity, auditability, competitive cost) that determine which risks survive in self-authored frameworks, finding that harmful manipulation is fluently disclosed where law compels it but systematically absent from companies' self-chosen risk accounts.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.18357: Capability-Based Planning for AI Crisis Preparedness — A Government Methodology Framework
entries.summary: The paper adapts defense and homeland security capability-based planning to AI threats, arguing that likelihood-based risk assessment fails for AI (since expert timelines disagree by orders of magnitude) and proposing instead a scenario library, per-capability rating procedure, and decision-rule prioritization matrix — piloted across the four most severe AI-enabled threat classes.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.19737 (TempJail): Subtitle-Scheduled Temporal Jailbreaks Against Video LLMs Beat Prior Attacks by 53pp on GPT-5
entries.summary: TempJail constructs dialogue-style subtitle sequences and optimizes their temporal scheduling to exploit timing vulnerabilities in large vision-language models, achieving the highest attack success rate across all evaluated model-dataset settings and outperforming the strongest prior baseline by 53 percentage points on GPT-5 and 18 on Gemini 3.5-Flash.

entries.title: arXiv 2608.19266: OWASP LLM Top 10 Expert Ranking vs. 7,714-Incident Corpus Shows Weak Agreement (Cohen's κ≈0.20)
entries.summary: Two OWASP GenAI working-group members (non-official) validate the 2026 Top 10 for LLM Applications against 6,639 labeled incidents from CVE, GHSA, OSV, and AIAAIC using a Bayesian measurement-error model, finding the expert and data-derived rankings agree only weakly — key evidence for calibrating AI security taxonomies used in audits and evaluations.

entries.title: Beazley Report: Agentic AI in Security Research Drives 36% Q2 2026 Quarter-Over-Quarter Surge in Disclosed Vulnerabilities
entries.summary: Beazley Security's August 2026 data show a 36% quarter-over-quarter rise in newly disclosed vulnerabilities in Q2 2026, attributed in part to agentic AI being used in security research, alongside a smaller but meaningful rise in actively exploited vulnerabilities — empirically documenting the dual-use acceleration dynamic.

entries.title: Azure DevOps MCP Server Lets Attackers Embed Prompt Injections Invisible to Humans Inside Pull Request Comments
entries.summary: ExploreSec researchers found that the Azure DevOps MCP Server reads attacker-controlled malicious instructions hidden in pull request comments in a form invisible to human reviewers but consumed by AI agents, creating a new prompt injection vector that undermines AI-assisted code review in DevSecOps pipelines.

entries.title: AI Slopsquatting Near-Miss: Hallucinated Package Name Nearly Installs Pre-Registered Malicious Package at Softjourn
entries.summary: A documented near-miss at software firm Softjourn shows that attackers pre-register packages under names AI agents commonly hallucinate (slopsquatting), turning developer trust in AI-recommended packages into a supply chain attack vector — stopped only by an existing policy requiring download-count verification before any AI-recommended installation.

entries.title: Binance Agent OS Launches Autonomous AI Trading With Oversight Gaps: Platform Cannot Observe Agent Reasoning or Detect Prompt Injection
entries.summary: Binance launched Agent OS, allowing AI agents to autonomously analyze markets and execute trades, but acknowledged it cannot observe agent reasoning or detect prompt injection attacks and relies primarily on user-configured sub-accounts for governance — a live example of agentic financial AI deployed without platform-level safety enforcement.
